newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African industrial shares ended slightly firmer, riding up on the back of an early rise on Wall Street and retracing the losses seen during most of an active day's trade, dealers said on Thursday.
"The industrials are closing on the up side, obviously the Dow has something to do with that. The Dow is up very, very strong," one dealer said.
Wall Street which fell by 20.87 points on Wednesday started up 40 points on Thursday, with dealers saying its cheerful start would probably firm Friday's trade.

"Trading has been fairly good today, but I wouldn't say over active. Tommorrow (Friday) is probably going to be flat to maybe slightly better. I'm just thinking of the Dow closing slightly better tonight," another dealer said.
The dealers said the market's underlying sentiment remained positive, but added that some local economic data expected to be released on Friday could hold sway on the market's future direction.
The March trade data, money supply and credit extension figures are largely seen as indicators for movements in the interest rates, they added.
The industrial index ended up 10.6 points to finish at 8,425.4, the gold index shed 1.3 points to close at 1,230.5 and the all-share index gained 7.7 points to 7,087.9.
Dealers said volumes were moderate on the day with around 685 million shares traded, adding the market had also taken a breather amid some positive gains since Monday.
"Our market has been very, very strong over the last couple of days. It's rebounded very well and I think it's finding new levels. It's going to go quiet and consolidate," a dealer commented.
The dealers said among stocks which saw some heavy trading on Thursday had been M-Cell which finished down 30 cents at 522 cents, after earlier touching a low of 440 cents.
They said a single bookover of some five million shares had later helped prop up the stock.
"The brokerage basically knocked the stock down all the way from 5.50 rand to 4.50 and did the bookover there," one dealer added.
While the industrials were responsive to Wall Street the golds remained stunted for most of the day with bullion still resisting any climb up the $340 an ounce level, dealers said.

They said sentiment from poor gold quarterlies, which the market has largely disounted, was still permeating through the nerves of some market players and leading them to shy away from the precious metal.

"The golds have been unconvincing. Basically trust is just not there, the gold price is not doing much, it's hovering around $340 level, it doesn't want to kick back into the $340-$345 range," a dealer said.
"But I think we are getting a lot of bad news out of the way so you might see in the short term a sort of a bounce in some of the gold shares," he added.

Anglo was one gold mining house which dealers said failed to spur some positivity when it said on Thursday its gold mines had available profit of 224.3 million rand in the quarter to end-March, 34 percent down on the previous quarter.
Anglo shed 500 cents to 303.00 rand and Goldfields lost 50 cents to close at 112.00 rand.
Gold contracts hardly budged on Thursday, dulled by the tamed bullion price.
The June industrial contract was last at 8,270/75 from 8,270 settlement, the gold contract at 871/80 from 868 and the all-share contract at 6,565/90 from 6,583 settlement.
-- Ellis Mnyandu, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
